what_is.title: What is ARFID?
what_is.subtitle: Essential facts about Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder.
what_is.def_p1: is an eating disorder in which an individual significantly restricts the volume and/or variety of foods consumed.
what_is.def_p2: Far beyond simple picky eating; it is a clinical condition that can lead to malnutrition, weight loss, or marked impairment in daily social functioning.
what_is.distinction_title: Not About Body Image or Weight Concerns
what_is.distinction_intro: Unlike anorexia or bulimia, food restriction in ARFID is strictly unrelated to:
what_is.distinction_1: Body perception or body shape concerns
what_is.distinction_2: Fear of weight gain or becoming overweight

who.title: Who Gets It?
who.subtitle: ARFID can affect individuals of any age and across diverse health backgrounds.
who.card1_desc: Occurs in both children and adults; it is not limited solely to early childhood.
who.card2_desc: More frequently observed in individuals with Autism spectrum, ADHD, and anxiety disorders.
who.card3_desc: Higher prevalence among individuals experiencing digestive conditions (such as celiac disease).
who.card4_desc: Prevalent across boys, men, and diverse gender identities; not exclusive to any single gender.

symptoms.title: Symptoms & Subtypes
symptoms.subtitle: ARFID is typically categorized into 3 core subtypes accompanied by physical and social symptoms.
symptoms.type1_desc: A general lack of interest in eating, unawareness of internal hunger cues, and prolonged meal durations.
symptoms.type1_b3: Lack of appetite and low food volume
symptoms.type2_desc: Pronounced selectivity driven by heightened sensitivity to textures, smells, colors, and tastes.
symptoms.type2_b3: Relying on a restricted pool of 'safe foods'
symptoms.type3_desc: Food avoidance rooted in a past traumatic experience (choking, vomiting, allergic reactions, etc.).
symptoms.type3_b1: Fear of choking, gagging, or vomiting
symptoms.type3_b2: Reluctance to try unfamiliar or solid foods

treatment.title: Treatment & Therapy Process
treatment.subtitle: There is no one-size-fits-all formula for ARFID; personalized and multidisciplinary approaches are essential.
treatment.card1_desc: No single treatment fits everyone; most individuals make meaningful progress through tailored combined therapies.
treatment.card2_desc: The primary modality is CBT-AR, an adaptation specifically targeting sensory and anxiety-driven eating mechanisms.
treatment.card3_desc: Physicians, specialized dietitians, and psychologists/psychiatrists collaborate closely throughout recovery.
treatment.card4_desc: Particularly in children and adolescents, family-centered therapeutic models demonstrate high efficacy.
treatment.card5_desc: Recovery pace varies individually; progress occurs gradually and sustainably under professional guidance.
treatment.card6_desc: Without coercion, the safe food repertoire is slowly expanded while respecting sensory tolerance limits.

diagnosis.title: Important Notice: Diagnostic Procedure
diagnosis.quote: "ARFID can only be diagnosed by a qualified healthcare professional (physician, psychiatrist, or psychologist) after comprehensive clinical assessment. This platform is not a diagnostic tool."
diagnosis.subtext: If you suspect eating difficulties, please consult an accredited medical institution and specialist without delay.

assistant_sec.title: How Our Assistant Helps
assistant_sec.subtitle: A supportive digital companion designed to make your daily nutritional journey reassuring and manageable.
assistant_sec.card1_desc: Gradually learns your safe and avoided foods as well as sensory triggers (texture, smell, temperature) to offer customized guidance.
assistant_sec.card2_desc: Draws upon a reliable RAG knowledge base to suggest comforting recipes fully aligned with your sensory profile.
assistant_sec.card3_desc: Equipped with calorie and portion estimates, sensory fit scoring, and trigger food queries to assist your everyday choices.
assistant_sec.disclaimer_text: This assistant DOES NOT replace a dietitian or medical doctor and does not provide clinical diagnoses — it serves solely as a supportive nutritional companion.
